slides.0.title: Winemaking and Style
slides.0.subtitle: From steel to oak, and sweet-wine production
slides.1.title: The Assyrtiko spectrum
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Dry white
slides.1.highlights.0.content: At least 85% Assyrtiko and often 100%; lees maturation and oak are optional, not required
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Nykteri
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Dry, at least 13.5% ABV and at least 3 months in oak
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Vinsanto
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Sun-dried over-ripe grapes (at least 370 g/L sugar), at least 51% Assyrtiko and at least 24 months of oxidative maturation
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Acidity and pH
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Retains high acidity at full ripeness; on potassium-poor volcanic soils pH can fall to 2.7–2.8
slides.1.content: Assyrtiko outside Santorini shows more primary fruit with a less dense, more mineral structure (WineWithSeth).
slides.2.title: Xinomavro: traditional versus modern extraction
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Traditional
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Long maceration, built for long cellaring
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Modern
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Cold soak and gentler extraction, emphasising fruit
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Naoussa ageing tiers
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Standard: at least 1 year in oak; Reserve red: at least 3 years in total with at least 6 months in oak; Grand Reserve: at least 48 months in total (24 in oak + 24 in bottle)
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Declassification
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Naoussa must be 100% Xinomavro; adding any other grape means declassification to Imathia PGI or Macedonia PGI
slides.2.content: A Diploma comparison: explain why one grape has traditional and modern winemaking philosophies, and how regulation intervenes.
slides.3.title: Winemaking notes for aromatic whites and reds
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Moschofilero
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Bone-dry with racy acidity, typically 11–12.5% ABV; rose water, jasmine, honeysuckle, grapefruit and stone fruit
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Malagousia
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Richer than Moschofilero yet with good acidity; peach, mango, citrus and jasmine
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Agiorgitiko
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Rosé, light young reds, oak-aged Reserve and even sweet styles
slides.3.content: Write winemaking as cause and effect: choice (maceration, oak, lees) → style outcome (structure, aroma, ageing potential).
slides.4.title: Retsina, sweet and fortified production
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Retsina
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Aleppo pine resin is added during fermentation and removed afterwards; capped at about 1% (10 g/L) and added before about two-thirds of fermentation; PGI Retsina needs at least 85% Savatiano (WineWithSeth)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Mavrodaphne of Patras
slides.4.highlights.1.content: At least 51% Mavrodaphne (the rest Black Corinthian); at least 1 year in oak; Reserve is 2 years in oak plus 1 in bottle; Grand Reserve 7 years in total
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Samos
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains; Vin Doux, Vin Doux Naturel, Grand Cru, Anthemis and Nectar (sun-dried grapes)
slides.4.content: Three questions for sweet-wine production: where does the sweetness come from, is it fortified, and is ageing oxidative or reductive?
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
What is the minimum Assyrtiko share in Santorini PDO dry white?
Per the official Wines of Greece PDO page it is at least 85%, with Athiri and Aidani at most 15% together.
What happens if a non-Xinomavro grape is blended into Naoussa?
A. It is declassified to Imathia PGI or Macedonia PGI
B. It is upgraded to Grand Reserve
Naoussa is a 100% Xinomavro single-variety PDO.
What does the Nykteri rule require?
A. At least 13.5% ABV and at least 3 months in oak
